topic: Lifecycle & ViewModel internals: owners, stores & scopes

questions.question: How does a ViewModel survive rotation of its Activity?
options: It is serialized into the saved instance Bundle and rebuilt
Android pauses the Activity instead of recreating it when any ViewModels exist
The ViewModel holds a reference to the Activity and re-attaches itself
Its ViewModelStore is retained across the change and returns the same instance
questions.explanation: ComponentActivity hands its ViewModelStore across the configuration change as a non-configuration instance, so the new Activity gets the same store. ViewModelProvider then finds the existing instance by key. Nothing is serialized, which is why ViewModels don't survive process death.

questions.question: viewModelScope is cancelled when the ViewModel is cleared, which happens when its ViewModelStore is cleared.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: viewModelScope is tied to the ViewModel's clearing: when the owning store clears it, the scope is cancelled as part of that clearing, along with its running coroutines. Work that must outlive the screen belongs in an application-level scope or WorkManager.

questions.question: A Fragment collects a Flow using `lifecycleScope` / `this` as the owner in onViewCreated. What bug appears after the user navigates away and back?
options: The Flow is never collected because the Fragment is not started at that point
Each new view starts another collector while old ones keep running
The Fragment crashes because lifecycleScope is cancelled in onStop
Only the first emission is received, then the Flow stops
questions.explanation: A Fragment on the back stack keeps living while its view is destroyed and recreated. Tying collection to the Fragment's lifecycle means each new view starts another collector while older ones (touching dead views) keep going. Use viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope with repeatOnLifecycle.

questions.question: What does `repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { flow.collect { ... } }` do?
options: Starts the block once at STARTED and keeps it running until DESTROYED
Pauses the collector below STARTED but keeps the upstream Flow active
Runs it at STARTED, cancels it below, and reruns it on return
Runs the block every time an ON_START event is sent, never cancelling it
questions.explanation: repeatOnLifecycle launches the block when the lifecycle reaches STARTED and cancels it when it drops below, then relaunches when it's back. Cancelling stops the upstream too, which is why it replaced launchWhenStarted, which only suspended the collector and kept producers running.

questions.question: Which statements about how ViewModels are created are true? Select all that apply.
options: Factories receive CreationExtras, which can include the Application and default arguments
Inside a viewModelFactory initializer, createSavedStateHandle() builds a handle tied to the owner's saved state
ViewModelProvider can build classes with arbitrary constructor parameters by reflection, without a factory
Passing a different key lets one ViewModelStore hold two instances of the same class
Every viewModel() call during recomposition creates a fresh instance
questions.explanation: Factories get context through CreationExtras, and createSavedStateHandle uses the owner keys inside them. Instances are stored by key, so a custom key gives a separate instance, while the same key returns the existing one on each call. The default factory only handles no-arg (or AndroidViewModel-style) constructors.

questions.question: A LifecycleObserver is added to a Lifecycle that is already RESUMED. What does the observer receive?
options: Nothing until the next event, such as ON_PAUSE
Only ON_RESUME, since that is the current state
ON_CREATE, ON_START and ON_RESUME, in order
A single ON_ANY event describing the current state
questions.explanation: LifecycleRegistry brings new observers up to the current state by dispatching each missed event in order. That's why code in ON_START/ON_CREATE observers still runs when added late. Relying on only seeing future events is a common misconception.

questions.question: ProcessLifecycleOwner sends ON_STOP with a short delay after the last Activity stops, so a configuration change doesn't look like the app went to the background.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: During rotation the old Activity stops before the new one starts. ProcessLifecycleOwner waits briefly before dispatching ON_PAUSE/ON_STOP, so if a new Activity starts in that window no background event fires. ON_START and ON_RESUME are sent without delay.

questions.question: In ComponentActivity, what decides whether the ViewModelStore is cleared when ON_DESTROY happens?
options: Whether it is being destroyed for a configuration change
Whether onSaveInstanceState was called before onDestroy
Whether any of the ViewModels still has coroutines running in viewModelScope
Whether the system is low on memory at that moment
questions.explanation: On ON_DESTROY, ComponentActivity clears its store unless isChangingConfigurations is true, in which case the store is handed to the next instance. onSaveInstanceState is called in both cases, so it can't tell them apart, and running coroutines never keep a ViewModel alive.

questions.question: Which statements about ViewModels and lifecycles in Compose are true? Select all that apply.
options: viewModel() uses LocalViewModelStoreOwner, such as an Activity, Fragment or NavBackStackEntry
Each composable that calls viewModel<FeedViewModel>() gets its own instance
If the calling composable leaves the composition, the ViewModel lives on until its owner's store is cleared
Inside a NavHost destination, LocalLifecycleOwner is that destination's NavBackStackEntry
viewModelScope is cancelled when the composable that called viewModel() is disposed
questions.explanation: viewModel() looks up the nearest owner and returns the instance stored under that class/key, so callers under the same owner share it. Its life follows the owner's store, not the composable, so disposal of the caller doesn't clear it. NavHost provides each entry as both the ViewModelStoreOwner and LifecycleOwner.

questions.question: What is the key difference between collectAsStateWithLifecycle() and collectAsState() in a composable?
options: The lifecycle version stops collecting below STARTED
The lifecycle version caches the last collected value across process death
collectAsState only works with StateFlow, not other Flows
The lifecycle version collects on a background thread
questions.explanation: collectAsStateWithLifecycle collects only while the LifecycleOwner is at least STARTED (by default), so upstream work stops when the app is in the background. collectAsState keeps collecting as long as the composable is in the composition. Neither saves values across process death.
